motions.motion_text: Deputy Mayor Gray moved, seconded by Morzel to approve consent agenda items 3A through 3K with items 3A and 3F amended and item 3D pulled from consent and taken up as a public hearing later in the meeting.
motions.vote_text: The motion carried 8:0 with Appelbaum opposed to item 3G.

motions.motion_text: Council Member Wilson moved, seconded by Osborne to adopt Ordinance No. 7658 amending the requirements related to the protection of wetlands, including Sections 9-3-9, “Wetlands Protection,” 9-16-1, “General Definitions,” and 4-20-53, “Wetland Permit and Map Revision Fees,” B.R.C. 1981, by repealing, reenacting and adopting by reference the wetlands maps of the city of Boulder and the wetlands functional evaluations and setting forth related details.

Council Member Morzel moved, seconded by Espinoza to adopt Ordinance No. 7651 enacting a new Chapter 2-2.5, B.R.C. 1981 addressing civil emergencies and disasters, establishing authority and procedures to take specified actions in the event of a disaster emergency and setting forth related details.

Council Member Gray moved, seconded by Morzel to adopt substitute Ordinance No. 7552 adopting and approving an Intergovernmental Agreement between Boulder County, the City and County of Broomfield, the Cities of Boulder, Lafayette, Longmont, and Louisville, and the Towns of Erie and Superior, relating to the management of hazardous materials; and its Exhibit A found in Attachment B.

Council Member Ageton moved, seconded by Gray to adopt Resolution No. 1051 in support of enhancing collaborative efforts between the Boulder Valley School District, the University of Colorado at Boulder, Boulder County and the City of Boulder to progress toward environmental sustainability; as amended to add “diverse and inclusive” prior to “work force” on page 6 of the agenda memo.

Council Member Cowles moved, seconded by Appelbaum to ratify the Board and Commission appointments. Council appointed Paul Saporito to a five-year term on the Downtown Design Advisory Board and Thomas Krueger to a five-year on the Board of Zoning Adjustment.

Mayor Appelbaum moved, seconded by Morzel to appoint Council Member Morzel with Deputy Mayor Gray as alternate to the Kisumu Sister City Committee and appointing Council Member Wilson as representative to the Yamagata Sister City Committee.

open_comment_speakers.name: Lenna Kottke
open_comment_speakers.topic: Opportunity to provide additional services with grant funds and urged adoption of item 3E.

open_comment_speakers.name: Sam Alschuler
open_comment_speakers.topic: Spoke regarding Orchard Grove and the angst that exists in the Park given the uncertainty of its future with the continued rent increases.

open_comment_speakers.name: Seth Brigham
open_comment_speakers.topic: Spoke to the suggestion of creating a living wage for council but why not a living wage for the community?

open_comment_speakers.name: James McClements
open_comment_speakers.topic: Spoke of the proposed collaboration with CU and BVSD. He suggested a way to bring together BVSD, the City and residents to address traffic problems related to Foothills Elementary School.

open_comment_speakers.name: Robert Webb
open_comment_speakers.topic: Neighbor of Foothills Elementary School, spoke in support of developing a strategic and inclusive process for a Foothills Elementary safety plan.

open_comment_speakers.name: Stephen Keenan
open_comment_speakers.topic: Voiced support for concerns expressed by the Foothills Elementary parents and neighbors. He suggested forming a separate school district for the city.

open_comment_speakers.name: Rob Smoke
open_comment_speakers.topic: Commended staff for the good job it does (noted 28th and Pearl as an example). He urged finding a way to save libraries; possibly cutting salaries is a way to keep the community whole.

open_comment_speakers.name: Robert Sharpe
open_comment_speakers.topic: Spoke of the challenges facing Boulder due to the changing values of the city's elected officials and corrupt city staff.

open_comment_speakers.name: Sarah Schulte
open_comment_speakers.topic: A Foothills Elementary parent indicated how grateful they are to have such a wonderful school. The frustration comes from a process that was no process. There was no community input allowed in making a safety decision which will result in the removal of over ½ of the green area without considering other options.

open_comment_speakers.name: Callie Weiant
open_comment_speakers.topic: Spoke regarding a work plan for the revitalization of University Hill. She voiced her support for the initiative as there is tremendous potential for improvements.

open_comment_speakers.name: Morgan Rogers
open_comment_speakers.topic: Representing PLAN Boulder County spoke in support of the direction of the Climate Action Plan but would like to hear how the plan will address the goals before supporting a tax increase.

open_comment_speakers.name: Michael Rowe
open_comment_speakers.topic: Spoke to restoring the Pioneer Train. He asked council to take action to support this effort.

open_comment_speakers.name: Lynn Segal
open_comment_speakers.topic: Spoke to the need to delay the opening of the Comanche III Coal Plant.

open_comment_speakers.name: Sam Alschuler
open_comment_speakers.topic: Orchard Grove resident, indicated that the 5-acre parcel is not covered by the Wetlands Ordinance because the ditch was man made (note – over 100 years ago).

open_comment_speakers.name: Barrett Weisz
open_comment_speakers.topic: Addressed the Greenbelt Meadows mosquitoes issue. He noted that the city is incredibly lucky to have an extraordinary staff that has been completely responsive in moving this forward.

open_comment_speakers.name: Barb Kostanick
open_comment_speakers.topic: Spoke as an effected property owner urging council to adopt the ordinance. It had been a long and painful process over 4 years. This would be a huge step forward.

open_comment_speakers.name: Gail Gordon
open_comment_speakers.topic: Expressed that she is still concerned that the “right to build or rebuild in perpetuity for current owners and future owners” is still not in the ordinance.

open_comment_speakers.name: David W. Crumpacker
open_comment_speakers.topic: Shadow Creek Condominiums, requested that a permit not be required to rebuild a structure with its existing footprint.

open_comment_speakers.name: Buff Elting
open_comment_speakers.topic: 25 year resident, stressed that people who live by the creek value the aesthetics of this neighborhood. He also requested the ability to rebuild.

open_comment_speakers.name: Mary Nakashian
open_comment_speakers.topic: Shadow Creek Condominiums, thanked the Planning Board and Planning staff for all the hard work in drafting the proposed Ordinance. However, she agreed with previous speakers’ comments that no permit should be required and regarding the right to rebuild for current and future owners in perpetuity.

open_comment_speakers.name: Phoebe Greyson
open_comment_speakers.topic: Also asked that clear language be added to clarify the right to rebuild in perpetuity for current and future owners.

open_comment_speakers.name: Bob Rubino
open_comment_speakers.topic: Arapahoe resident, echoed concerns of other neighbors. All of the neighbors support protecting the creek but it has become impossible to do anything in their back yards. He requested council not adopt the Ordinance in its current form.
